subject: Linguistics
title: Conventional Implicature
description: A short lesson to help you apply Conventional Implicature.

hook.text: 'She's rich but kind.' The word 'but' implies that rich people aren't usually kind.

buildup.text: Conventional implicatures are triggered by specific words—'but,' 'even,' 'yet,' 'still.'

discovery.text: Unlike conversational implicatures, they're built into the word itself—not calculated from context.

twist.text: They can't be cancelled: 'She's rich but kind—and I don't mean that's surprising' still sounds contradictory.

climax.text: Conventional implicatures live in the gray zone between semantics and pragmatics.

punchline.text: Some words carry hidden messages baked right into them.
